card.name: Zwiefacher
card.era: Term first documented 1780; older melodies predate the modern bar line
card.tagline: Bavarian couple dance with changing meter.
card.profile: The Zwiefacher is a southern German couple turning dance with quick tempo and changing meter, alternating between 3/4 (waltz) and 2/4 (Dreher/pivot) - and occasionally polka - beats, in regular or irregular patterns. Couples turn rapidly in a closed (often barrel) hold. It is danced mainly in Lower Bavaria, the Hallertau and the Upper Palatinate, and is also known in the Black Forest, Austria, Alsace, the Czech Republic and Sudetenland. Accompaniment is accordion, fiddle and brass; lyrics served as mnemonics. Researcher Felix Hoerburger catalogued 112 tunes carrying 474 different names (English Wikipedia).
card.insight: The name (loosely 'twofold'/'double') may refer to the two alternating meters or to the couple being tightly wound together; the dance was added to Germany's Nationwide Inventory of Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2016 (English Wikipedia).
